title: Everest Base Camp vs Annapurna: Which Should You Visit?
verdict: For those chasing a globally recognized peak, the Everest Base Camp trek offers unparalleled bragging rights and a singular focus on altitude. categories.name: h2 id="getting-there-logistics">✈️ Getting There & Logistics

categories.name: h2 id="scenery-landscapes">🏞️ Scenery & Landscapes

faq.question: Do I need a guide for Everest Base Camp or Annapurna?
faq.answer: While it's technically possible to trek independently on most Annapurna routes (Circuit, ABC), a guide is highly recommended for both due to safety, navigation, and local insights. For EBC, recent regulations often require a licensed guide for foreign trekkers, and it's certainly safer given the altitude and remoteness.

faq.question: What kind of permits do I need?
faq.answer: For EBC, you'll need the Sagarmatha National Park entry permit and a local Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality entry fee. For Annapurna, you'll require an Annapurna Conservation Area Permit (ACAP) and a Trekkers' Information Management System (TIMS) card. All can be obtained in Kathmandu or Pokhara.

faq.question: How long do these treks typically take?
faq.answer: A standard Everest Base Camp trek from Lukla typically takes 12-14 days round trip, including acclimatization days. The full Annapurna Circuit is a longer commitment, usually 14-21 days, while the Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) trek is shorter, about 7-12 days.

faq.question: What's the highest point on each trek?
faq.answer: The highest point on the Everest Base Camp trek is Everest Base Camp itself, at 5364 meters (17,598 ft), or Kala Patthar at 5550m. The highest point on the Annapurna Circuit is Thorong La Pass, at 5416 meters (17,769 ft). Annapurna Base Camp is at 4130 meters (13,550 ft).

faq.question: Is Acute Mountain Sickness (AMS) a serious concern?
faq.answer: Yes, AMS is a very serious concern on both treks, especially EBC and Thorong La Pass. Proper acclimatization, slow ascent, staying hydrated, and recognizing symptoms are crucial. Never ignore symptoms and always descend if they worsen. Consult your doctor before your trip.

faq.question: What should I pack for these treks?
faq.answer: Essential gear includes a good quality sleeping bag (rated to -10°C / 14°F), sturdy trekking boots, layers of warm clothing (down jacket, fleece), waterproof outer shell, hat, gloves, headlamp, water purification, and a basic first-aid kit. Porters can carry your main pack (typically 15-20kg limit).

faq.question: Can I do these treks during the monsoon season?
faq.answer: EBC is generally not recommended during monsoon (June-August) due to heavy rain, leeches, and unreliable Lukla flights. The Annapurna Circuit, however, has parts (like the Manang valley) that fall into a rain shadow, making it a viable (though challenging in lower sections) option for a unique monsoon trek.

faq.question: Are there good side trips or alternative routes?
faq.answer: Absolutely! For EBC, popular side trips include the Gokyo Lakes trek or crossing the high passes (Cho La, Renjo La). For Annapurna, highly recommended side trips include Tilicho Lake (on the Circuit) or combining the ABC trek with Poon Hill for sunrise views. Both regions offer incredible extensions.
